exact_feasibility_theorem.name: Custodian-nondelegation upper bound
exact_feasibility_theorem.proof_obligation: Evaluate the custodian/delegation conjunct for each of the twelve unchanged V8 groups and independently recompute the upper bound from the result table.
exact_feasibility_theorem.scope: Exact for this frozen registry and source library; not a claim that a future owner-signed algebra is impossible.
exact_feasibility_theorem.statement: For a frozen conjunctive registry G, let sufficient(g,S) require source coverage, applicable rights, exact schema coverage, and named-custodian authorship or explicit delegation. If a source library S contains no named-custodian authorship or explicit delegation for g, then sufficient(g,S)=false. Therefore the maximum number of sufficient groups is the count of groups whose custodian conjunct is evidenced, regardless of lexical action-token coverage.

owner_group_sufficiency.cannot_check: Missing public access is the only reason a group does not pass.
owner_group_sufficiency.negative: All twelve fail at least one observed conjunct with no access uncertainty relevant to that failure.
owner_group_sufficiency.positive: One or more of the unchanged twelve groups passes every conjunct.
owner_group_sufficiency.rule: A V8 requirement group is sufficient only when every existing V8 discriminator is met, exact R7 target coverage/exhaustiveness is present where required, applicable reuse rights are bound, and the named required custodian or explicit delegation is evidenced. Partial public-standard analogues contribute zero sufficient groups.

scaffold_feasibility.cannot_check: Identity or exact bytes cannot be bound for enough sources.
scaffold_feasibility.negative: Fewer than three independent accessible institutional families expose an explicit native postpublication token.
scaffold_feasibility.positive: At least three independent institutional source families are byte-bound and expose explicit native postpublication action/status or relation tokens; at least one source distinguishes a content status/action from a linking relation or policy role.

scientific_action_gold.positive: Only an owner-separated adjudication receipt over eligible cases may create a nonzero count; public standards alone are inadmissible.

native_token_gateway.no_semantic_crosswalk: A lexical or source-native action/status token is not mapped to any R7 decision or treated as scientific-action gold.
native_token_gateway.retention: For prose sources retain only existence booleans and exact allowlisted terms, not sentences. For schema/tag sources retain exact enumerated tokens and local element/attribute names.

prohibitions: No self-assigned R7 owner identity or delegation
No host execution or recommendation authority inferred
No owner ratification or independent review fabricated
No manuscript, ledger, PDF, Git history, commit, push, merge or rebase operation
readiness_rule: P1 readiness changes only if scientific-action gold becomes nonzero and all authority, rights, custody and construct gates required by the current readiness matrix are bound. A standards scaffold or exact zero-group upper bound alone cannot change readiness.
scientific_question: Can the strongest accessible public authority-native postpublication standards supply a lawful, source-native action/terminal scaffold and, under the unchanged V8 conjunctive custodian rule, make any of the twelve R7 owner-algebra requirement groups sufficient without case text, outcomes, or self-assigned authority?

source_capture_rule.fail_closed: HTTP non-2xx, identity mismatch, parse failure, or ambiguous semantics is CANNOT_CHECK; never substitute a search snippet or third-party copy.
source_capture_rule.method: One HTTP GET with an identifying research User-Agent, redirects followed, 30 second timeout; record requested URL, final URL, UTC capture time, HTTP status, content type, content length, ETag, Last-Modified and SHA-256 of exact response bytes.
source_capture_rule.raw_retention: No raw HTML or PDF in the final packet. Temporary source bytes must be deleted after hashing and bounded extraction.
